topics.preferred: Decided representation: unidentified follow-up work must have a null object ID; the discussion episode remains #26586. The recurring retention criterion likewise needs no numbered proposal ID. A null inapplicable identifier does not make its semantically identified assent target unknowable. I prefer ordinary, tentative assent to this proposition: the quotation preserves the recurring non-EOL floor, while the surrounding exchange supplies the wallet-testing domain and the floor entails retaining qualifying releases rather than substituting them. The omission of words from a quotation alone does not prove narrower assent.
topics.alternatives: The strongest alternative is recognition of the proposed minimum as a governing consideration, with an unresolved recognition profile. A broader-principle target is also defensible if the omitted no-substitution formulation is treated as independently material. Neither reading establishes adoption, repeated recognition, or binding authority.
topics.unresolved: The force of the tentative assent remains interpretive under v0.4. Future-work identity is unknown; criterion identity is semantically recoverable although a canonical numbered ID is inapplicable. These are different uncertainties.

topics.preferred: The later open-and-rebase suggestion maintains the method but does not repeat the earlier stopping condition. Narrow S13 recognition to broader_principle. Prefer same_actor_only wherever an attributable same_actor_restatement is retained, including the review-now strategy: the codebook expressly assigns same-actor events that profile, and does not make interpersonal recognition or established obligation prerequisites. This summary records maintained personal commitment, not recognition by another participant. The existing S13-to-S22 uptake direction can remain, with its limited response rationale.
topics.alternatives: The strongest profile alternative is none for the partial open-PR event, if the summary is restricted to full-proposition recognition. That restriction is less clearly stated for recognition than for application. The review-now restatement is materially closer to its complete focal intention and therefore supplies a stronger case for same_actor_only.
topics.unresolved: No uncertainty permits reinstating the omitted dependent-PR stopping condition or treating either repetition as interpersonal support. The scope of the profile for broader-target same-actor events remains a convention ambiguity.

topics.preferred: Prefer observed application of the requested resulting spelling. The added release-note heading and matching integrated revision establish that artifact without reconstructing the earlier typo or attributing causation. The checkbox evidence is different: it establishes a prepared checkbox artifact but not every placement and functional qualification of the complete proposition. Prefer unresolved complete application, while preserving the narrower artifact observations already recorded in outcomes. An unmerged patch can still be observed; lack of integration alone is not a reason to deny observation of a proposed artifact.
topics.alternatives: A transformation-specific spelling interpretation can retain unresolved application of the historical correction operation. It should not displace the separately observable resulting identifier. For the checkbox, none is a defensible no-positive-application summary, but unresolved communicates the partial evidence and outstanding qualifications more accurately.
topics.unresolved: The spelling history and exact checkbox placement remain unverified. No new partial-application category or before-and-after requirement should be added to v0.4.

topics.preferred: Prefer context-inferred reported application for the three release-note suggestions. The author attributes the update to the reviewer’s changes, and the reviewer identifies the suggested release-note updates. This is an intelligible collective report about those suggestions; reporting need not individually enumerate every item. It does not resolve the isolated fixed or Both replies, verify verbatim implementation, or prove adoption of every rationale. By contrast, rebasing on master neither names nor establishes the after-#26589 condition. Retain that broader rebase report and mark complete conditional application unresolved.
topics.alternatives: A broader_proposal target for the aggregate report is defensible where collective reference is considered insufficient to identify individual suggestions. This is a genuine scope interpretation, not necessarily a substantive error. Its cautiousness alone does not make it preferable.
topics.unresolved: The individual reply antecedents, the omitted compatibility rationale, and the dependency chronology remain unverified. Reported and observed application must retain their distinct evidentiary meanings.

topics.preferred: Prefer undetermined institutional type with norm_candidate retained for both rebase formulations. A pragmatic maintenance request is supported, but these words alone do not discriminate a social expectation from a technical condition for maintaining the contribution. Recommendation is a reasonable pragmatic force; unresolved force remains appropriate when the literal technical-necessity reading is focal. The absence of authority defeats a rule-candidate inference, but cannot itself decide between a proposed norm and an ordinary engineering request.
topics.alternatives: The strongest alternative is norm_candidate: an elliptical reviewer demand can express locally expected contributor conduct even without repetition or wider assent. Requiring a recurring or already shared expectation would add a criterion that v0.4 explicitly does not require.
topics.unresolved: Retain the type ambiguity rather than treating either interpretation as established by needs. No executed rebase, institutional obligation, or authority follows merely from the phrasing.

topics.preferred: Two analytical layers should remain explicitly linked. For the embedded add-every-release instruction and script-edit action, I prefer operational targets with collective-choice observed deliberation. For the constitutive up-to-the-developer allocation, I prefer a collective-choice target: it proposes who will select releases under a recurring arrangement. A pragmatic developer-chooses representation can instead target the resulting operational conduct. These differences should be explained through the selected proposition rather than labeled as disagreement about authority.
topics.alternatives: Treating the whole design proposal as choosing a recurring testing arrangement supports collective_choice for both target and observation. Conversely, ordinary engineering deliberation remains an operational observation alternative. The source does not uniquely settle whether every technical selection arrangement is institutional at that layer.
topics.unresolved: Constitutive parsing does not imply constitutional power. No statement allocates control over Bitcoin network adoption. Both layers are supportable within v0.4; linked explanations are preferable to uniform labels imposed without changing focal meaning.

topics.preferred: Q019: for an offered checkbox proposal, the exposure objection challenges its readiness premise, so prefer this_proposition and dispute_present true. A challenge need not deny the physical checkbox to contest offering it under the stated conditions. Q038: retain focal dispute over the specialness justification, preferably premise. Q039: retain the challenge to the explicitly attached miniscript rationale, without inferring #25717 contents. Q040: a proposed redesign addresses the burden of the current requirement but does not refute its current technical truth; prefer a broader-proposal application challenge and no focal dispute. Q052: the fee-only alternative does not dispute the historical attempt.
topics.alternatives: For Q019, a strictly artifact-descriptive focal proposition supports broader_proposal and false. For Q040, a prospective challenge to continued application can support true if that prospective layer is explicit. These are bounded focal-object alternatives, not opposing facts.
topics.unresolved: The unobserved future workflow and proposed redesign remain unadopted possibilities. No disagreement with past work or actual implementation should be inferred from an alternative future method.

topics.preferred: Reverse the separate-cleanup uptake relation to initiating proposal U30 followed by response U33. For the quoted cost-growth question, prefer clarifies from the pruning option to the concern: the reply directly addresses an append-only premise without requiring an inferred request. For release-risk speculation followed by hold-off assent, prefer a contextual clarifying response about intended handling, with the weak thread evidence stated. No relation establishes that a delay or pruning occurred.
topics.alternatives: Uptake remains defensible when the cost question is reconstructed as a request for a removal plan, or the release concern as an implicit delay proposal. That reconstruction must be explicit. Context record status alone does not prove that no pragmatic request occurred, but neither does a responsive utterance automatically establish one.
topics.unresolved: The direction of P04 is decided by v0.4. The other relation types remain interpretive; quotation establishes response correspondence more strongly in Q042 than the unthreaded sequence establishes it in Q043.

topics.preferred: Retain the bot’s announced reaction-to-next-update consequence, but leave the software object unresolved. The pronoun it is an explicit grammatical object; its referent is not therefore explicit. Review is a plausible antecedent, while comment or displayed listing cannot be excluded from this retained wording. The known PR discussion ID does not resolve which software object the bot would ignore.
topics.alternatives: The incorrectly listed review is the strongest ordinary-language reading, and can be recorded as an alternative rather than asserted categorically. A specific implementation interpretation would require evidence absent from the packet.
topics.unresolved: No reaction, update, suppression, executed sanction, or implemented governance consequence is observed. Preserve that limit alongside the conditional statement.

topics.preferred: Prefer strategy_candidate for the specific-test preference: it articulates a testing method and examples, although no personal implementation commitment follows. Prefer strategy_candidate for the coupled EOL-drop and stored-wallet alternative, whose components jointly specify a replacement testing method. Splitting the clauses must preserve that coupling. Prefer norm_candidate for not rushing merges: it offers a reason for expected restraint in recurring integration conduct. None of these classifications establishes shared acceptance, authority, or implementation.
topics.alternatives: Undetermined remains strongest for a mere evaluative preference or tentative one-off suggestion. The not-rushing sentence can likewise be read as optional practical advice rather than expected conduct. These alternatives remain stronger than inferring a rule from modal force or reducing every technical method to an institutional norm.
topics.unresolved: V0.4 leaves a judgment boundary between articulated method, technical suggestion, and proposed social expectation. Preserve the preferred types and explicit alternatives without turning classifications into evidence of collective recognition.

topics.preferred: Use null for unidentified follow-up contributions and for a general criterion without a canonical object; #26586 identifies the discussion episode. Sjors gives tentative ordinary assent. In context, his selected quotation can identify the wallet-retention proposal, including the non-substitution implication, without repeating every word. I therefore prefer this_proposition with context-inferred scope, while keeping recognition none under the ordinary-assent interpretation. The quotation identifies what he agrees with; it does not independently show that he treats it as a governing consideration. Correcting object identity is decided; the semantic breadth of assent is less certain.
topics.alternatives: Broader-principle assent is defensible because the selected quotation omits the wallet-specific framing and explicit non-substitution clause. Tentative expectation recognition also remains possible; neither reading warrants repeated recognition, binding authority, or adoption.
topics.unresolved: Null is inapplicable for the general criterion, unknown for a future contribution. An unidentified future proposal requires an unresolved target only when that proposal itself is the event target; semantically identified general-principle assent need not become unresolved.

topics.preferred: The later open-PR proposal repeats a method, not the earlier condition until another PR needs it. Retarget S13 to broader_principle. For the review-now statement, the same author explicitly maintains the distinction between present review and unfinished replacement work. Preserve these response events and their same_actor_restatement mode, while retaining recognition none in the corrected views. The frozen checker filters to expectation_recognition of this_proposition before calculating same_actor_only; the existing events are responses, not demonstrated expectation recognition. Do not change their kind merely to obtain a different summary label.
topics.alternatives: The codebook sentence that same-actor events alone give same_actor_only supports a broader prose reading, including maintained personal commitment. That interpretation cannot presently be applied consistently with the frozen checker, particularly for broader-principle method repetition.
topics.unresolved: This is a concrete codebook/checker tension: check_annotation.py profile() lines 33–45 imposes a kind-and-target filter absent from the standalone prose sentence. Preserve the maintained-commitment finding in event records and the decision overlay. None here describes the existing projection, not absence of attributable continuity or evidence of interpersonal recognition.

topics.preferred: The integrated release-note artifact directly shows the requested spelling. Observed application, explicitly limited to the resulting spelling, is justified without a new before-and-after requirement. The prior typo, correction chronology, and causal response remain unverified. For the checkbox, the supplied patches directly show a checkbox and connected sequence-setting code. Lack of merge does not negate this prepared artifact. However, placement next to Add Recipient is not shown by the retained patch context, so full-proposition application remains unresolved. Preserve the observed artifact in the existing outcome record rather than inventing a partial-application category. The author’s supplied report and the technical artifact are different evidence types; neither turns the absent adjacency context into a verified placement claim. The complete proposal should not silently become a narrower checkbox-only proposition merely to secure an observed label.
topics.alternatives: An artifact-limited observed checkbox event could be defensible if its scope is unmistakable. An unqualified observed profile for the complete proposition would obscure the unverified placement; none also hides an actually examined, relevant artifact.
topics.unresolved: The schema lacks a partial application status. This representational limitation remains; integration is a separate disposition, not a universal prerequisite for observing an offered patch.

topics.preferred: The author explicitly reports updating the PR with the reviewer’s changes; the reviewer corroborates release-note updates suggested above. This supports context-inferred reported incorporation of the identified suggestions, not merely an unspecified PR update. Prefer this_proposition for that limited report, with independent patch observations kept separate. It does not resolve fixed or Both, verify every tentative phrase, or prove adoption of a rationale. Conversely, rebasing on master establishes only the reported rebase: no text connects it to satisfaction of after #26589. Retain the broad report and a separate unresolved full-condition assessment.
topics.alternatives: Broader-proposal targeting of aggregate reports remains defensible under a stricter itemization reading. That ambiguity should not erase the positive correspondence between the named reviewer, changes, and corroborated release-note update.
topics.unresolved: Exact local reply pairings and the specified dependency event remain unknown. The omitted backward-compatibility phrase cannot be treated as verified verbatim implementation.

topics.preferred: Prefer undetermined for the terse rebase comments because their supplied context does not distinguish technical necessity from socially expected contribution work. Retain norm_candidate as a serious alternative: a local maintenance request can propose an expectation without repetition or prior acceptance. Recommendation and unresolved force are defensible parses; neither entails obligation. The r1 #7819 rationale should stop treating lack of a recurring expectation as decisive, because v0.4 permits proposed case-specific norms.
topics.alternatives: Norm_candidate is reasonable when the review utterance itself is interpreted as an expectation directed at the contributor. Nothing supplies authorized merge-gate status, and the word needs cannot furnish that missing evidence.
topics.unresolved: The technical-need/social-expectation boundary cannot be made categorical without additional criteria. Preserve existing preferred labels with explicit alternatives rather than declaring either label erroneous.

topics.preferred: Keep operational performance and choosing a recurring arrangement as explicitly linked analytical layers. Adding releases or selecting locally available test versions describes operational conduct; proposing that these become the recurring selection arrangement supports collective-choice analysis. The developer-choice sentence preserves conditional allocation under either constitutive or pragmatic regulative grammar. The selected level must follow the stated focal proposition, not a general rule that all recurring code behavior is governance. Existing rationales mostly identify their layers; do not overwrite their differences with a single level.
topics.alternatives: Ordinary engineering review remains a supported alternative for the directory-loop exchange. Collective-choice deliberation is stronger for the explicit every-major-release criterion, but still proves neither adoption nor power allocation above testing conduct.
topics.unresolved: v0.4 allows both editorial/proposal and embedded-conduct layers. Comparisons must state which is focal; no constitutional or network-authority conclusion follows. The conditional phrase In that case must remain attached to developer discretion under either grammatical decomposition; unconditional authority would change the proposition.

topics.preferred: Q019: for the offered checkbox feature, the exposure objection challenges its readiness premise, so prefer this_proposition and dispute true; it does not deny the artifact. Q038: retaining both versions despite no specialness challenges the explanation requirement’s premise, not merely its wording. Q039: the miniscript objection challenges that attached rationale only; it cannot adjudicate unseen #25717 or every reason to add v24. Q040: a future directory-loop redesign does not falsify the present fixed-list prerequisite; prefer no identified challenge to the present technical claim. Q052: prospective fee-only self-questioning leaves the historical additional-output attempt uncontested. Its broader scope alternative can remain visible.
topics.alternatives: A literal checkbox-presence report supports broader-proposal targeting and false dispute; make that focal layer explicit. The directory-loop response can alternatively challenge continued application of the prerequisite if the claim is construed as ongoing, rather than current-implementation necessity. These alternatives concern represented objects and temporal scope, not an invitation to settle disputes by choosing whichever Boolean produces more agreement.
topics.unresolved: The substantive targets, not Boolean agreement, carry the result. Readiness, a particular technical premise, continued applicability, and future scope are distinct disputes.

topics.preferred: Reverse the cleanup uptake link: proposal U30 precedes response U33 in the relation’s semantic direction. For the quoted cost-growth concern, prefer clarifies from the pruning response to the concern because the initiating unit remains context and makes no explicit request. For release-withdrawal speculation, prefer temporal linking to the separate pause proposal: the frozen timestamps establish order, while reliable reply threading and an initiating delay request are absent. Preserve the topical connections without implying implementation or causation.
topics.alternatives: The cost question can pragmatically invite a plan; an uptake link is defensible if that invitation is stated explicitly. Sounds good also supports an implicit-invitation reading, but its exact initiating proposal remains less securely identified.
topics.unresolved: Direction is a decided convention correction. Uptake versus clarifies or temporal remains a contextual interpretation; no formal hold, release withdrawal, or completed pruning is observed.

topics.preferred: Keep the literal object it and qualify its referent. The likely review interpretation is an inference; comment or displayed-listing interpretations remain possible from the text alone. The bot announces a conditional next-update effect after a reaction to this comment. This supplies neither execution nor a uniquely identified internal software object. Correct categorical referent claims wherever they are repeated, including summary, qualifier, institutional rationale, and target-activity description.
topics.alternatives: The incorrectly listed review is linguistically plausible as the antecedent and may remain the preferred gloss, but no supplied implementation evidence eliminates the comment/listing alternatives.
topics.unresolved: The underlying software referent is agreed uncertainty. Grammatical Bdir it is explicit even though its referent is unresolved; do not turn referent uncertainty into an inferred-object-role correction.

topics.preferred: Prefer strategy_candidate for the specific-test preference: it identifies a testing approach and recoverable examples, rather than only an unexplained edit. The coupled EOL-drop/retained-wallet proposal more clearly articulates means for prioritizing old-wallet loading; preserve both halves and their substitution relation. Neither method requires a firm personal commitment under v0.4. Prefer norm_candidate for not rushing new-release merges when read as proposed recurring restraint, with undetermined retained for a case-specific timing rationale. The stated merging action is explicit even though recommendation force is inferred; use literal parse for that action rather than inventing avoid-rushing roles.
topics.alternatives: Specific-test preference can remain an engineering preference without enough method articulation; undetermined is defensible. The restraint sentence can give a possible reason without asserting expected conduct. None of these type labels demonstrates shared norms or implementation.
topics.unresolved: Type thresholds leave bounded interpretation choices; literal action versus inferred recommendation force is separately governed by the existing parsing convention.

topics.preferred: Separate three objects. The proposed recurring retention floor has no applicable numbered proposal identifier; the prospective cleanup has an unknown identifier; #26586 identifies the discussion episode. Null therefore has different explanations. Tentative agreement demonstrably concerns the quoted recurring floor. I prefer unresolved expectation recognition, rather than deciding that ordinary assent is the only supported reading: the quoted language itself articulates a continuing standard, but Sjors does not explicitly apply it as governing conduct. A this_proposition target is defensible because the wallet context and no-substitution implication remain recoverable from the exchange, even though not repeated verbatim.
topics.alternatives: Ordinary_assent with recognition none remains defensible. Broader_principle is also defensible if the omitted wallet-specific and no-substitution wording is considered material to assent scope. Neither reading licenses interpersonal recognition as an established finding, repeated recognition, or adoption.
topics.unresolved: Identity corrections are decidable. Recognition threshold and complete-proposition assent remain v0.4 ambiguities. Null event IDs denote inapplicable identifiers for general principles; preserve #26586 as independence_key. The recommended recognition replacements are preferences, not compelled error repairs.

topics.preferred: The open-and-rebase passage repeats a method, not the condition until another PR needs it. Narrow S13's event accordingly. For the review-now statements, same_actor_only best follows v0.4's express summary convention: an attributable actor maintains a personal approach across occurrences. The convention does not say that such an event must first establish a social expectation. I also prefer that profile for the broader-method repetition, with its narrower target visible.
topics.alternatives: None is defensible for the fully conditional open-PR proposition if profile scope excludes broader-principle events. It is less persuasive for the directly corresponding review-now statements. Do not assume the retained PR-body wording chronologically preceded the comment.
topics.unresolved: Partial correspondence is decidable; broader-event projection into the recognition profile is ambiguous. Same_actor_only never establishes interpersonal recognition or shared normative standing.

topics.preferred: Observed application is warranted for the requested spelling as a resulting artifact: v0.4 expressly permits observation of an artifact. It does not require reconstruction of the earlier typo. F02_S01 can therefore report both application dimensions when its aggregate-report interpretation is retained. The checkbox differs: an artifact is visible, but placement beside Add Recipient and the complete workflow qualification are not independently established by that fragment. Prefer unresolved application of the complete checkbox proposition, preserving the observed feature facts separately.
topics.alternatives: A historical correction-operation focal object supports unresolved observation. A deliberately narrower checkbox-feature object could support observed application, but silently replacing the existing qualified proposition would change the analytical object.
topics.unresolved: Transformation history remains unknown. The checkbox's unmerged status does not negate artifact observation, and artifact observation does not establish integration. v0.4 provides no dedicated partial-application profile.

topics.preferred: The aggregate update report can contextually include the reviewer's three identified documentation suggestions. The follow-up review's reference to updates suggested above strengthens that mapping; requiring an individually itemized report would introduce a new rule. Retain r1's reported this_proposition interpretation, bounded to the requested edits rather than every proposed phrase. For rebasing, retain reported action on the PR and unresolved fulfillment of the complete after-#26589 request as separate records.
topics.alternatives: Broader_proposal targeting for aggregate reports remains defensible, so r2/r3 need no mandatory changes on Q006. Neither aggregate report determines what fixed or Both refers to. The rebase profile none can mean no established complete application, but unresolved communicates the available partial evidence more accurately.
topics.unresolved: No supplied dependency record connects #26589 to master at that rebase. Report scope is interpretive; dependency satisfaction is an evidence gap.

topics.preferred: Prefer undetermined for both rebase formulations. A review-context request is identifiable, but this source does not select between social accountability and technical maintenance necessity. The after-#26589 qualification improves timing specificity, not the evidence of institutional obligation. Recommendation force and undetermined type can coexist.
topics.alternatives: Norm_candidate is defensible when the utterance is interpreted as publicly expecting the contributor to perform maintenance. It need not be repeated, shared, or project-wide. Retain that possibility explicitly, including where currently omitted; do not erase the existing r2 norm candidate solely to impose agreement.
topics.unresolved: Technical versus social force cannot be resolved from needs alone. Lexical-D transfer and Cac/Cex choices remain bounded parsing alternatives, not evidence of a merge gate or authority.

topics.preferred: Retain linked layers. The instruction to add releases and the developer's ordinary selection activity target operational conduct. Proposing a recurring release-selection arrangement, including shifting selection from hardcoding to local availability, targets collective_choice. The visible exchange plausibly deliberates that arrangement, without adopting it. Conditional developer choice can receive a constitutive allocation parse, provided its condition and unchanged download default survive.
topics.alternatives: A regulative description of technical configurability is equally defensible for developer choice. An operational observed-action reading remains possible where the focus is engineering review rather than selection of an institutional procedure. The level follows the stated analytical layer; labels alone should not collapse the alternatives.
topics.unresolved: No constitutional power, network authority, or adopted procedure follows. Primary level changes are unnecessary where the existing rationale clearly identifies its layer.

topics.preferred: Q019: prefer a broader-proposal readiness challenge when the focal object is the prepared checkbox artifact; exposure and review are distinct. Q038: retain dispute true, preferably premise: the response rejects specialness as necessary justification while favoring verification of presumed similarity. Q039: retain the miniscript premise challenge to the qualified inclusion argument; it does not refute unseen #25717 or all reasons for v24. Q040: prefer a broader arrangement challenge and false focal dispute because redesigning the test does not contradict its present built-copy prerequisite. Q052: the historical attempt remains uncontested; the fee-only question concerns future workflow scope.
topics.alternatives: A checkbox offer understood as exposing the feature supports a focal sequencing challenge. A built-copy requirement understood as a continuing arrangement supports an application challenge under v0.4's workaround provision. These alternatives require explicit focal scope. The explanation response could also be construed as supplying a justification rather than contesting the criterion.
topics.unresolved: Challenge Booleans are projections of focal scope. Preserve alternatives without converting them into rejection, withdrawal, contradiction of historical work, or interpersonal disagreement with oneself.

topics.preferred: P04 requires reversal if uptake is retained: the separate-cleanup proposal precedes its attributable scope response. For Q042, prefer clarifies from pruning option to quoted cost concern because the initiating record remains contextual questioning. Q043 offers weaker response attribution: a temporal sequence with the separate pause proposal is preferable to a firm uptake inference.
topics.alternatives: The directly quoted Q042 concern plausibly invites explanation, permitting context-inferred uptake without causal adoption. Q043 uptake is also defensible if the rationale expressly identifies the inferred invitation; the proposed rationale makes that interpretation reviewable. Context status alone does not disprove a communicative response.
topics.unresolved: P04 direction is decidable. The other relation preferences depend on inferred invitation, not an observed removal, release withdrawal, formal delay, or causal effect.

topics.preferred: The mislisted review is a plausible antecedent, not a uniquely established software object. Preserve the conditional next-update response while qualifying the summary, scope note, and propagated descriptions. Bdir it is an explicit grammatical object even though its referent remains uncertain.
topics.alternatives: The relevant object could be the review, the comment, or its displayed listing. None can be selected by assuming how the unseen bot implementation works.
topics.unresolved: Software identity is an evidence gap. Keep the announced consequence distinct from observed execution.

topics.preferred: Prefer strategy_candidate for the specific-test preference and coupled EOL-drop/stored-wallet alternative. Both articulate methods, and v0.4 does not require every method to contain a personal undertaking. The second especially identifies a means of pursuing the stated old-wallet compatibility priority; preserve both actions and their substitution relationship. Prefer norm_candidate for not rushing integration: it proposes restraint on recurring contribution conduct and offers a checking rationale, although acceptance remains unestablished.
topics.alternatives: Undetermined remains defensible if these are treated as one-off engineering preferences or a rationale for this particular pause. A preference alone does not establish accountability. The absence of authorization excludes a rule finding but cannot by itself exclude strategy or norm candidates; the generic r3 rationale therefore supplies an incomplete type justification.
topics.unresolved: These are bounded type preferences, not shared norms, implemented methods, or duties to abandon every EOL test. Preserve exploratory force and inferred storage roles; no primary type convergence is mandatory.
